flagged.evidence: The local definition says processes are indistinguishable when “the event {X_t=Y_t for every t∈I} is measurable and has probability one.” Proof 4.1 establishes equality on a measurable probability-one event, then concludes “Thus the versions are indistinguishable.” The statement does not assume a complete probability space, and the cited continuous-version theorem explicitly notes that on a noncomplete space the full equality set may fail to be measurable. Equality on a measurable full event therefore does not establish the defined indistinguishability claim.
